question.text: `Jeevan Jyoti Foundation`, a public charitable trust in Maharashtra running rural ICU services, is primarily governed by which of the following?

answer.text: Indian Trusts Act 1882 — because all trusts in India fall under this Act
Societies Registration Act 1860 — because charitable trusts must register as societies
Companies Act 2013 Section 8 — because charitable purpose mandates the Section 8 route
Bombay Public Trusts Act 1950 — because it is a public charitable trust operating in Maharashtra

explanation.text: The Logic: The Indian Trusts Act 1882 applies to private trusts. Public trusts generally follow the law of the relevant state; in Maharashtra and Gujarat, public trusts have their own state law - the Bombay Public Trusts Act 1950 - which is therefore the primary governing statute for a Maharashtra-based public charitable trust like Jeevan Jyoti Foundation. The Trap: Option A overstates the reach of the 1882 Act, which does not cover public trusts. Option B conflates the trust form with the society form. Option C treats Section 8 as compulsory for charitable purposes when it is just one of several available legal forms. Note: Public trust statute of the relevant state is also a qualifying NPO registration route for Social Stock Exchange purposes.
